cohort: The cohort consisted of 159 pregnant women with singleton pregnancies and gestational age over 30 weeks, presenting to antenatal clinics with suspicion of intrauterine growth restriction.
finding: The Doppler scan showed high sensitivity (83.3%), specificity (93.3%), and diagnostic accuracy (91.8%) in detecting intrauterine growth restriction.
cross-section timing: Doppler scans were performed during pregnancy (after 30 weeks gestation) and compared against intrauterine growth restriction status at birth.
gest_age: Gestational age more than 30 weeks (inclusion criteria); mean gestational age at delivery was 35.3 (± 0.95) weeks.
